input: In a cardiopulmonary support literature search, expand ECMO. Give synonyms or spelling variants of the support modality itself.
For venovenous ECMO, list the hyphenated and spaced spellings and the short form with a space before ECMO.
For venoarterial ECMO, list the hyphenated and spaced spellings and the short form with a space before ECMO.
For right ventricular dysfunction, suggest literature-search wording, including an abbreviated adjectival phrase and a phrase using the chamber noun.
In the context of oxygen-carrying blood protein, give American and British spellings of the generic protein name.
Expand AKI in a renal critical-care search. Include only its spelled-out contemporary diagnosis.

Journal article. Investigators randomly assigned 84 adults to two rehabilitation schedules and report measured walking distances for both arms.
Conference abstract. People were randomly allocated to morning or evening physiotherapy. The authors report outcomes for both groups.
Journal article. This protocol describes a planned randomized comparison in adults. Recruitment has not begun and no outcomes are available.
Journal article. Reviewers systematically searched for trials of rehabilitation in adults, assessed eligibility in duplicate, and pooled published estimates in a meta-analysis.
Journal article. Investigators used archived records from a cohort of 210 adults to conduct a new analysis of their outcomes after hospital discharge.
Conference abstract. We describe the course and follow-up of one adult patient after rehabilitation.
Society web document. The issuing panel presents its clinical practice guideline for adult rehabilitation. Recommendations synthesize prior literature. The panel collected no new data.
Journal article. Adults were enrolled before discharge and followed for a year to measure new events. Rehabilitation was chosen by their clinicians.
Journal article. At one clinic visit investigators recorded symptoms and walking distance from 120 adults. There was no follow-up.
Journal article. Investigators performed semi-structured interviews with adult patients and present a thematic analysis of the transcripts.
Conference abstract. The only information supplied is the title, 'New perspectives on rehabilitation'. Methods, population and results are unavailable.
Journal article. This case series describes four dogs referred for rehabilitation, with individual measurements before and after treatment. No human subjects were studied.
